thesis: Ben Savage argues that the distinction between public and private markets is an artifact of post-Depression regulation and that the future of investing will shift from liquid, regulated markets to historically less liquid and less regulated ones. He posits that technology is driving liquidity into these previously inaccessible segments while regulations are peaking, meaning that over the next 20 to 50 years, the majority of market capitalization and value will likely reside in what are currently considered private markets.
